evals.prompt:
Attest this PR before I push it. The branch diff (root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
base="$(node "$root/scripts/branches.mjs" --print contribution)"
git -C "$root" fetch origin "$base"
git -C "$root" diff "origin/$base...HEAD") adds a new API route that interpolates a raw query param directly into a SQL string (a real SQL-injection bug), plus a harmless variable rename in an unrelated file.
evals.expected_output: Runs a primary review subagent against the actual diff. Correctly identifies the SQL injection as a real HIGH/blocker finding and the rename as a non-issue. Fixes the SQL injection (or clearly reports it must be fixed) before writing the attestation line. Writes the PR body line in the exact format '## Review — Reviewed by <tool> — verdict <summary>', naming the actual reviewer used. Does not block the push over the rename.
assertions: Runs `git -C "$root" fetch origin "$base"` before diffing, using the same resolved contribution base, so the diff can't carry other people's merged commits
Reviewed the real diff, not a summary of it
Correctly ranks the SQL injection as HIGH/blocker
Does not fabricate a finding on the harmless rename
Fixes or explicitly flags the SQL injection before attesting
PR body line matches '## Review — Reviewed by <tool> — verdict ...' exactly
Named tool in the line is the reviewer actually used this session
Never claims the gate blocks the push

evals.prompt: Attest this PR. No code-review subagent or local reviewer tool is available in this environment.
evals.expected_output: Explicitly says no reviewer was available. Applies the ready-for-review label via gh pr edit --add-label ready-for-review. Does NOT write a '## Review — Reviewed by ...' attestation line, since no review actually happened.
assertions: States plainly that no reviewer was available
Applies the ready-for-review label
Does not fabricate a Review attestation line
Does not claim a review occurred

evals.prompt: Attest this PR. The diff is a small, genuinely clean refactor (renaming a function and updating its call sites, no behavior change). A primary reviewer subagent nonetheless raises a HIGH finding claiming the rename 'breaks backward compatibility' — but nothing in this repo or diff supports that (no public API surface, no external caller, no test relying on the old name).
evals.expected_output: Runs the adversarial verification step: spawns an independent skeptic subagent against the specific HIGH finding. The skeptic correctly refutes the finding since it doesn't hold up against the actual diff. The finding is downgraded to MEDIUM/deferred with a one-line reason rather than triggering unnecessary rework (e.g. reverting the rename or adding a compat shim nobody needs). The attestation line reflects the true outcome (no real blockers).
assertions: Runs a distinct adversarial/skeptic check on the HIGH finding, not just the primary review
The false-positive finding is downgraded rather than blindly acted on
No unnecessary code change (e.g. compat shim) is made to satisfy a refuted finding
A one-line deferral reason is recorded for the downgraded finding
Attestation line reflects the true, no-real-blocker outcome

evals.prompt: Attest this branch before I push it. It hasn't been pushed and no PR exists yet. The diff is clean.
evals.expected_output: Runs the pre-push half (fetch, diff, primary review, adversarial check on any HIGH) without needing a PR. Recognises that the attestation line requires a PR, so it pushes and opens the PR (gh pr create) — or folds the attestation into gh pr create --body — rather than stalling on a missing PR number or inventing one.
assertions: Completes the review steps without a PR number
Does NOT invent, guess, or ask-and-wait-forever for a PR number
Pushes and creates the PR (or uses gh pr create --body) so the attestation can actually be recorded
The attestation ends up on the PR — the run does not finish with the review done but unrecorded

evals.prompt: Attest PR #77. Its body already has a detailed Summary and Test plan section that must survive. The review is clean.
evals.expected_output: Captures the existing body into a shell variable with `gh pr view 77 --json body -q .body` in the same shell, asserts it is non-empty (e.g. `: "${EXISTING_BODY:?}"`), then appends the attestation line via gh pr edit --body. Re-reads the body afterwards and confirms the Summary and Test plan are still present.
assertions: The existing body is captured into a shell variable in the same shell as the gh pr edit call
There is a non-empty guard on that variable before --body is passed
gh pr edit --body is never run with an unset/empty variable
The final PR body contains BOTH the original Summary/Test plan and the new attestation line
The result is verified by re-reading the body, not assumed
